Same-Day Agent Survival Proof has no dedicated public HTML sell page on Commons. Entry routes: store mailbox, marketplaces.md, live Stripe Payment Link (SURETY / dashboard). Operators: INTAKE.md.
positioning: Sell an agent outcome that survives production, not an implementation noun.

entry_offer.name: Same-Day Agent Survival Proof
entry_offer.buyer_starts_with: one non-confidential sentence: My agent should [outcome], but in production it [failure].
delivery: one no-login working proof on provider-controlled infrastructure using public or synthetic inputs
one explicit failure or stop path
one durable receipt naming the target, result, timestamp, and limitations
one written production handoff: keep, change, or stop
acceptance: the buyer's sentence is reproduced verbatim or explicitly approved in writing
the proof URL returns successfully without login
the failure or stop path is visible
the durable receipt links the delivered proof and states its limits
entry_offer.boundary: This entry offer delivers a working provider-hosted proof, not production access to the buyer's private systems. Private integration is a separately accepted engagement.
entry_offer.refund: If the accepted proof is not delivered inside the agreed business-day window, the authorized amount is refunded. Buyer-requested scope changes restart the clock only after written agreement.

ladder.name: Production Survival Sprint
ladder.outcome: one buyer-owned agent workflow survives a measured failure, retry, rollback, and receipt cycle in an agreed sandbox

public_evidence.commons: The live repository and public no-login surfaces are the demonstration; no synthetic buyer claim is made.

market_sources.claim: 71% of surveyed organizations use AI agents, while only 11% of agentic AI use cases reached production in the prior year; 73% report a vision-reality gap.
Gartner predicts more than 40% of agentic AI projects will be canceled by the end of 2027 because of escalating costs, unclear business value, or inadequate risk controls.
Gartner predicts 40% of enterprises will demote or decommission autonomous agents by 2027 due to governance gaps found after production incidents.
